prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right broker depends on your age, health, budget, whether you need family coverage, whether you want an HSA, and whether you want help with ACA subsidies or small‑business options. I can help find a good fit, but first a few quick options and actionable next steps.

Quick options
- Use a certified navigator/agent through HealthCare.gov (Missouri uses the federal marketplace). These helpers are free and experienced with subsidy eligibility and plan comparisons.
- Use a reputable online broker comparison site if you prefer doing it yourself: HealthSherpa, eHealth, Policygenius, or Stride (popular with freelancers). They compare multiple carriers and show subsidy effects.
- Hire a local independent health insurance broker/agent in Kansas City who: is licensed in Missouri, works with multiple carriers (independent, not captive), has ACA and self‑employed experience, and provides ongoing support for claims and renewals.

How to choose a good broker
- Verify license: check the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance license lookup.
- Ask whether they are independent (can quote many carriers) or captive to one insurer.
- Ask about fees/compensation (most get commission from carriers; some may charge a fee).
- Confirm experience with the ACA marketplace, subsidies, and options for the self‑employed (HSAs, QSEHRA/ICHRA if you have employees).
- Request 3–4 plan quotes, details on provider networks, out‑of‑pocket maximums, and prescription coverage.
- Read reviews (Google/Yelp) and ask for client references or case examples like yours.

If you want, I can
- Look up well‑rated Kansas City brokers/agencies for you (I’ll need your ZIP code and whether you’re in Missouri or Kansas side of KC).
- Compare 2–3 plan options based on your age, household size, and budget.

Which would you prefer — I can find local broker contacts or run some plan comparisons if you give me ZIP code, ages, and whether you want individual or family coverage.
